newsitem.title: USA: December sales stronger for most retailers.
newsitem.headline: December sales stronger for most retailers.

text.p: Most of the nation's retailers said Thursday their December sales rose as planned as consumers, cheered by the economy's strength, gave themselves a treat a year after one of the worst shopping seasons ever.

But while larger department stores seemed to be gaining market share, some discounters continued to fare poorly amid intense competition, especially with five fewer shopping days from Thanksgiving through Christmas in 1996 than a year ago.
Sears, Roebuck & Co. was among the best performers, with total U.S. store revenues for the five weeks ending Jan. 4 soaring 14.6 percent to $4.28 billion from $3.74 billion in the year-ago period.
Comparable domestic store revenues grew 9.5 percent, versus a 6.8 percent increase in the same period a year ago.
"We experienced record sales in December, including our first ever back-to-back billion-dollar sales weeks," said Arthur C. Martinez, chairman and chief executive of Sears.

"The outstanding performance of our full-line stores was led by double-digit increases in all our softline categories -- women's, men's and children's apparel, shoes, accessories, cosmetics, fine jewelry and home fashions -- and in computers, electronics, tools and hardware on the hardline side."
Sears Hardware and dealer stores generated double-digit comparable store increases, and gross margins were strong, the Hoffman Estates, Ill.-based company said.
Tiffany & Co. said its worldwide net sales in the Nov. 1 to Dec. 31 holiday season rose 15 percent over the 1995 period's sales.

The ritzy New York-based retailer said sales were led by strong performance in the United States and Japan, its two largest markets. Retail sales in the season rose 13 percent from the prior year in the United States, and surged 20 percent in Japan when translated into U.S. dollars.
Direct marketing sales rose 12 percent and international retail sales were up 17 percent, Tiffany said.
Kmart Corp. said same-store sales for the five-week period ended Jan. 1 rose 10.4 percent for its Kmart general merchandise and Builders Square stores.

Sales were led by the consumables area, followed by softlines and hardlines. Areas showing particular strength for the month included men's and children's apparel, fine jewelry, toys, sporting goods, housewares, electronics, consumables and cosmetics, it said.
For Kmart general merchandise stores in the United States only, same-store sales for the five-week period gained 11.6 percent, the Troy, Mich.-based retailer said.
Total sales for the five-week period rose 9.9 percent to $5.39 billion from $4.91 billion.
U.S. general merchandise sales for the five weeks gained 11.5 percent to $5.0 billion from $4.49 billion.

"Sales for the nine week period give the best indication of overall trends for the holiday season," said Floyd Hall, Kmart chairman, president and CEO. "On a comparable store basis for this period, our performance of 5 percent was ahead of plan."
Kmart has 2,141 Kmart and 168 Builders Square stores in the United States, and operates 129 stores overseas.
Dillard Department Stores Inc., with 253 traditional department stores in 24 states, said its same-store sales for the period ended Jan. 6 increased 4.4 percent.

Carson Pirie Scott & Co. said sales for the five weeks ended Jan. 4 rose 3.7 percent to $208.7 million from $201.3 million in the year-ago period. However, its comparable-store sales for the five weeks ended Jan. 4 fell 1.2 percent from a year ago.
"The five fewer days in the holiday selling season negatively impacted sales results for the month, said Stanton Bluestone, chief executive of the Milwaukee-based retailer.

United Retail Group Inc. also fared poorly, with total sales for the month ended Jan. 4 down 8 percent to $43.5 million from $47.5 million. Comparable store sales for the fiscal month slid 9 percent, it said.
United Retail, based in Rochelle Park, N.J., has 582 stores selling large-size women's clothing featuring The Avenue brand.
Limited Inc. posted unexpectedly poor December sales at its Express clothing store division, and warned of disappointing earnings for the year ending this month.
Limited, based in Columbus, Ohio, said it will announce several initiatives for 1997 in the next week.
